extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner procedures for entering, correcting, rejecting, and processing amendments (preliminary, supplemental, after-final, examiner's amendments) to U.S. patent applications under 37 CFR and MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendments (37 CFR 1.121(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may make amendments to the specification, including the claims, by examiner’s amendments without paragraph/section/claim replacement to expedite prosecution and reduce cycle time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additions or deletions may be made by instructions to change a precise location. Examiner's amendments do not need to comply with paragraphs (b)(1), (b)(2), or (c) of 37 CFR 1.121. The examiner’s amendment should include the reason why the amendment is non‑compliant and indicate how it was corrected. Authorization from the applicant or attorney/agent and extensions of time are not required if the changes are not substantive (e.g., format or typographical corrections). Authorization and appropriate extensions are required if changes are substantive (e.g., cancellation of a claim or change in claim scope) and must be given within the time period for reply set in the last Office action. See MPEP § 1302.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of status identifiers and entry of non-compliant amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a non-compliant amendment would otherwise place the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter the non-compliant amendment and provide an examiner’s amendment to correct the non-compliance (e.g., incorrect status identifiers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of correction methods: (A) provide a claim listing with proper status identifiers in an examiner’s amendment; (B) print the claim listing, cross out incorrect identifiers, handwrite correct identifiers and attach it to an examiner’s amendment; or (C) correct by instructions in an examiner’s amendment. Examiner’s amendment should state why the amendment was non-compliant and how corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and content for Non‑Compliant Amendments (Form PTOL‑324)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.121, the Office will notify the applicant by a Notice of Non‑Compliant Amendment (Form PTOL‑324) identifying the non‑compliant section, required items for compliance, and reasons for non‑compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The type of amendment determines whether a reply period is given and whether the reply may consist only of the corrected section (e.g., a complete claim listing) instead of the entire amendment. See the enumerated amendment‑type rules for specific time periods and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods and treatment for preliminary amendments filed after filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment filed after the filing date (but before the first Office action) that is non‑compliant will prompt TSS to send a notice setting a time period of 30 days or one month (whichever is later) for reply; no extensions allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely reply will result in the application being examined without entry of the preliminary amendment. Applicant’s reply must include the corrected section of the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods and treatment for preliminary amendments present on filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment present on the filing date that is non‑compliant will prompt OPAP to send a notice giving a two‑month time period for reply; extensions available under 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reply to the OPAP notice will result in abandonment of the application. Reply must include either a substitute specification under 37 CFR 1.125 (if amendment to the specification) or a complete claim listing under 37 CFR 1.121(c) (if amendment to the claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑final amendments (including those filed as an RCE) — notification and reply time
rubrics_metrics.description: For non‑final amendments (including an amendment filed as a submission for an RCE), TSS will send a notice setting 30 days or one month (whichever is later) for reply; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reply will result in abandonment or the application being examined without entry of the amendment as appropriate. Applicant’s reply must include the corrected section of the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: After‑final amendments — forwarding, non‑entry, and advisory action
rubrics_metrics.description: An after‑final amendment is forwarded in unentered status to the examiner; the examiner should indicate non‑compliance in the advisory action and attach a Notice of Non‑Compliant Amendment. The notice provides no new time period for correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time for reply continues to run from the mailing of the final Office action; applicant needs to respond to the final Office action to avoid abandonment. If applicant files another after‑final amendment, the entire corrected amendment (not only the corrected section) must be submitted within the time period set forth in the final Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental amendments (no suspension vs. within suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental amendment filed when there is no suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(a) or (c) will be forwarded to the examiner and is not entered as a matter of right. A supplemental amendment filed within a suspension period will prompt TSS to send a 30‑day or one‑month notice with no extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When no suspension, the examiner will notify applicant if the amendment is not approved for entry (may use form paragraph 7.147). When filed during a suspension period, failure to submit timely corrected section will result in examination without entry of the supplemental amendment. See 37 CFR 1.111(a)(2)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees for added claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment (including after‑final amendments) that adds new claims in excess of the number of claims previously paid for must be accompanied by payment of required excess claims fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay the excess claims fees will result in non‑entry of the amendment. See MPEP § 607.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments — defective directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Directions for entry of an amendment may be defective (e.g., inaccurate paragraph/page/line designation or lack of precision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the correct place of entry is clear from context, the amendatory paper will be properly amended in the Technology Center; the examiner will initial margin notation taking responsibility. In the next Office action the applicant should be informed of the alteration and entry. If defective directions and context leave doubt as to applicant's intent, the applicant will be informed of non‑entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of replacement paragraphs/sections (amendment of amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a replacement paragraph or section of the specification is to be amended, it should be wholly rewritten and the original insertion canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a marked‑up version using underlining to indicate added subject matter and strike‑through to indicate deletions. Matter canceled by amendment can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the canceled matter as a new insertion. A claim canceled by amendment may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatures to Amendments — who may sign
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment must be signed by a person having authority to prosecute the application; unsigned or improperly signed amendments are not entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Who may sign: (1) a registered patent attorney or agent of record appointed in compliance with § 1.32(b); (2) a registered attorney or agent not of record acting in a representative capacity under § 1.34; (3) an assignee as provided under § 3.71(b); or (4) all of the applicants (§ 1.41(b)), unless there is an assignee of the entire interest who has taken action under § 3.71. An unsigned or improperly signed amendment will be listed in the file but not entered; applicant given one month (37 CFR 1.135(c)) to ratify or supply proper signature. Applicants may be advised using form paragraph 7.84.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments signed by attorney/agent not of record or by applicant when attorney of record exists
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered attorney or agent acting in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34 may sign amendments even though not of record. If an amendment is signed by the applicant while a duly appointed attorney or agent of record exists, the amendment should be entered and acted upon, and copies sent to both the attorney and the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare two copies of the action, one to the attorney and one directly to the applicant; mark notation 'Copy to applicant' on original and both copies. See MPEP § 405 and § 714.01(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and publication effects of preliminary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment is one received on or before the mail date of the first Office action (37 CFR 1.115). For applications filed on/after Sep 21, 2004, a preliminary amendment present on filing date is part of the original disclosure; amendments filed after the filing date are not part of the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 (complete claim listing; each section begins on a separate sheet). Preliminary amendments to the specification (other than claims) may require a substitute specification in compliance with 1.121(b)(3) and 1.125 to be usable for publication. Filing a preliminary amendment is not recommended because changes may not be reflected in the patent application publication if technical preparations have begun. If present on filing date and containing subject matter not in the originally filed spec/drawings, applicant must file a supplemental oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.67 referring to the preliminary amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that preliminary amendments comply with 37 CFR 1.121
rubrics_metrics.description: Any preliminary amendment, regardless of when filed, must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 (e.g., include a complete listing of all claims and each section begin on a separate sheet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary amendments made only in a transmittal letter will not comply. If non‑compliant, applicant will be notified and given a one‑month non‑extendable period to bring the amendment into compliance (two months if present on filing date). Failure to correct will result in examination without consideration of changes (or abandonment if notice not answered).

rubrics_metrics.name: When preliminary amendments may be disapproved by the Director
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment in compliance with § 1.121 will be entered unless disapproved by the Director. It will be disapproved if it seeks cancellation of all claims without presenting any new or substitute claims, or if it unduly interferes with preparation of a first Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors in disapproval for undue interference: (i) state of preparation of first Office action as of receipt date; (ii) nature of changes to specification or claims. Entry will not be disapproved under 37 CFR 1.115(b)(2) if filed no later than: (A) three months from filing date under § 1.53(b); (B) three months from national stage entry under § 1.491; (C) three months from filing date of a CPA under § 1.53(d) for design apps; or (D) last day of any requested suspension period under § 1.103. These time periods are not extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors justifying denial of entry of a preliminary amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry may be denied when two conditions are met: (A) examiner has devoted significant time preparing an Office action before receipt; and (B) entry would require significant additional time to prepare the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of amendment content that may cause denial because they would require significant additional time: amends the claims; adds numerous new claims; amends the specification to change scope of claims; amends specification raising a new matter issue; includes arguments; includes an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131/1.132; includes evidence traversing rejections from a prior Office action in the parent application. This list is not exhaustive. Examiner should obtain SPE approval before denying entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: When disapproval of preliminary amendment entry is inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Denying entry under 37 CFR 1.115(b)(2) is inappropriate if either the examiner has NOT devoted significant time on the first Office action before receipt, or the entry would NOT require significant additional time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If either condition is not met, entry should not be denied; SPE approval is required if conditions for denial exist.
